cited_details.statement: The RecSys 2023 tutorial on *Large Language Models for Recommendation* (He et al., 2023) frames this transition as an evolution "from shallow models to deep models and to large models," arguing that formulating recommendation tasks as language instructions enables a *universal recommendation engine* capable of handling rating prediction, sequential recommendation, straightforward recommendation, and explanation generation within a single interface ([llmrecsys.github.io](https://llmrecsys.github.io/)).
The literature, as catalogued in the RecSys 2023 tutorial, organizes LLM-for-Rec methods along two main axes ([llmrecsys.github.io](https://llmrecsys.github.io/)):

A key enabling observation is that LLMs are *pre-trained on broad web-scale corpora*, which gives them open-domain knowledge that partially substitutes for the domain-specific training data required by classical recommenders (PremAI, 2024; [premai.io](https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/)).

**TALLRec** (Bao et al., 2023) proposes an *effective and efficient* framework built on parameter-efficient tuning (specifically LoRA-style adapters on a LLaMA backbone) to align an LLM with recommendation data ([arXiv:2305.00447](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.00447)).
The open-source release of TALLRec provides reference implementation details that practitioners can adapt ([GitHub: SAI990323/TALLRec](https://github.com/SAI990323/TALLRec)).

**Chat-Rec** (Gao et al., 2023), a collaboration between Fudan University, UC Davis, and Tongji University, addresses both by converting user profiles and historical interactions into *prompts* for a frozen LLM, augmented through *in-context learning* rather than fine-tuning ([arXiv:2303.14524](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2303.14524)).

The RecSys 2023 Late-Breaking Results paper **"Leveraging Large Language Models for Sequential Recommendation"** (Harald et al., 2023) explores how LLM-derived representations and language-based scoring functions can be exploited to model user intent over time ([DOI: 10.1145/3604915.3610639](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3604915.3610639)).

The associated code release confirms that the paper substantially extends an earlier RecSys submission and benchmarks the LLM-based approach against classical sequential baselines such as SASRec and BERT4Rec ([GitHub: dh-r/llm-sequential-recommendation](https://github.com/dh-r/llm-sequential-recommendation)).

(2023) provides a comprehensive taxonomy — *Naive RAG*, *Advanced RAG*, and *Modular RAG* — and describes how external retrieval from a knowledge base can be coupled to an LLM to mitigate these problems ([arXiv:2312.10997](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.10997)).

Across all four, the open-domain pre-training of LLMs is the unifying enabler, addressing the "domain-specific data" bottleneck of classical recommenders highlighted in the broader literature (PremAI, 2024; [premai.io](https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/)).

- **Latency and cost.** TALLRec's parameter-efficient design ([arXiv:2305.00447](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.00447)) and Chat-Rec's training-free prompting ([arXiv:2303.14524](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2303.14524)) each address cost in different ways, but industrial deployment at scale in latency-sensitive channels (in-app offers, contact-center prompts) remains non-trivial.

- **Latency and cost.** TALLRec's parameter-efficient design ([arXiv:2305.00447](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2305.00447)) and Chat-Rec's training-free prompting ([arXiv:2303.14524](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2303.14524)) each address cost in different ways, but industrial deployment at scale in latency-sensitive channels (in-app offers, contact-center prompts) remains non-trivial.

- **Reliability and hallucination.** The RAG survey ([arXiv:2312.10997](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.10997)) documents that RAG mitigates — but does not eliminate — hallucination; for regulated financial advice, additional guardrails are required.
